review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

11:1.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ προσευχόμενον, ὡς ἐπαύσατο, εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν Κύριε, δίδαξον ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ Ἰωάνης ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ.
11:1.targetText: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”

groups.note: The narrative formula Καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") is rendered One day, as in 9:18.
ἐν τῷ with the infinitive ("while he was") is recast as a where-clause about the place.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").
ὡς ἐπαύσατο ("when he stopped") is rendered had just finished.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτόν ("to him") implicit after requested.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated after just as.
BSB leaves εἶναι ("was") unexpressed; had just finished praying renders ὡς ἐπαύσατο with the participle.

11:2.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ὅταν προσεύχησθε, λέγετε Πάτερ, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου· ἐλθάτω ἡ βασιλεία σου·
11:2.targetText: So Jesus told them, “When you pray, say:  ‘Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come.

groups.note: BSB's Greek spells this same command form differently.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb.

11:3.sourceText: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν·
11:3.targetText: Give us each day our daily bread.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:4.sourceText: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν· καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν.
11:4.targetText: And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us. And lead us not into temptation.’”

groups.note: ὀφείλοντι ("who is indebted to") is rendered who sins against.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:5.sourceText: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον, καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ Φίλε, χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους,
11:5.targetText: Then Jesus said to them, “Suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,

groups.note: The question Τίς ("which of you …?") is recast as Suppose one.
ἕξει φίλον ("will have a friend") is rendered his friend.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB merges "has a friend and goes to him" into goes to his friend, so this καί and αὐτόν ("him") have no separate English.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit after says.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb.

11:6.sourceText: ἐπειδὴ φίλος μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ·
11:6.targetText: because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.’

groups.note: οὐκ … ὅ ("not … what") is rendered nothing.

11:7.sourceText: κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε· ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν· οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι.
11:7.targetText: And suppose the one inside answers, ‘Do not bother me. My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything.’

groups.note: κἀκεῖνος is καί ("and") with ἐκεῖνος ("that one").
ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ ("answering, says") is rendered answers.
κόπους πάρεχε ("cause troubles") is rendered bother.
The article is rendered with the possessive My.
οὐ δύναμαι ("I am not able") is rendered I cannot.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats the hypothetical frame of 11:5; the Greek continues with a subjunctive.
English supplies an object for give.

11:8.sourceText: λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι φίλον αὐτοῦ, διά γε τὴν ἀναιδίαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ὅσων χρῄζει.
11:8.targetText: I tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man’s persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs.

groups.note: The future δώσει ("he will give") is rendered with to provide after get up.
The articular infinitive τὸ εἶναι φίλον ("being a friend") is rendered friendship.
The particle γε ("at least") marks the contrast rendered yet.
ἀναιδίαν ("shamelessness") is rendered persistence; BSB's Greek spells the word differently.
αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered the man's for clarity.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐγερθείς, rendered get up, to the main verb.

11:9.sourceText: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν·
11:9.targetText: So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

groups.note: Κἀγώ is καί ("and") with ἐγώ ("I").

unmappedTarget.reason: English names what will be opened; the Greek has only the passive verb, as in Matthew 7:7.

11:10.sourceText: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει, καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει, καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
11:10.targetText: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB separates the first two statements with a semicolon instead of and.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names what will be opened; the Greek has only the passive verb, as in Matthew 7:8.

11:11.sourceText: τίνα δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς ἰχθύν, μὴ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει;
11:11.targetText: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?

groups.note: The article is rendered with the possessive his.
ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ("instead of a fish") is rendered instead.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated at the start of the question.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB's Greek has a different word here, and the English question renders neither word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English recasts the son's request as a condition; the Greek has no conditional word.

11:12.sourceText: ἢ καὶ αἰτήσει ᾠόν, ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον;
11:12.targetText: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated in the second question.

unmappedTarget.reason: English restates the conditional frame of the preceding question, as in Matthew 7:10.

11:13.sourceText: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
11:13.targetText: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”

groups.note: The article is rendered with the possessive your; Luke has no ὑμῶν here.
ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ("the one from heaven") is rendered in heaven.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:14.sourceText: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων δαιμόνιον, καὶ αὐτὸ ἦν κωφόν· ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι·
11:14.targetText: One day Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. And when the demon was gone, the man who had been mute spoke. The crowds were amazed,

groups.note: BSB renders the καί that opens this new episode as One day.
καὶ αὐτό ("and it") is rendered as the relative that.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula ἐγένετο ("it came about") untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb.

11:15.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπαν Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια·
11:15.targetText: but some of them said, “It is by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons, that He drives out demons.”

groups.note: BSB's Greek spells this same verb form differently.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English puts the means in a cleft sentence "It is by … that".
English puts the means in a cleft sentence "It is by … that".

11:16.sourceText: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρ’ αὐτοῦ.
11:16.targetText: And others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven.

groups.note: BSB makes παρ’ αὐτοῦ ("from him") the object of tested.

11:17.sourceText: αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται, καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει.
11:17.targetText: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτός ("he").
BSB repeats divided in the second clause, where the Greek leaves it understood.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:18.sourceText: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη, πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ; ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια.
11:18.targetText: If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? After all, you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.

groups.note: ὅτι ("because") is rendered After all.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ and καί ("also") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the reported statement; the Greek uses an infinitive.

11:19.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ ἔσονται.
11:19.targetText: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.

groups.note: English repeats the object as them in the second clause, where the Greek leaves it implicit.
διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered So then.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:20.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ Θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ.
11:20.targetText: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:21.sourceText: ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ·
11:21.targetText: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure.

groups.note: The generic article is rendered a.
ἐν εἰρήνῃ ("in peace") is rendered secure.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:22.sourceText: ἐπὰν δὲ ἰσχυρότερος αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν, τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφ’ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει, καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν.
11:22.targetText: But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτοῦ ("than him") implicit after stronger.
BSB says "the armor" and leaves αὐτοῦ ("his") implicit.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐπελθών, rendered attacks, to the main verb.
English names the subject for clarity; the Greek has only the verb ending.
English adds a time word to the final clause.

11:23.sourceText: Ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.
11:23.targetText: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.

groups.note: The article with the participle ὤν is rendered He who is.
The article with the participle συνάγων is rendered he who does … gather.

11:24.sourceText: Ὅταν τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται δι’ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ μὴ εὑρίσκον λέγει Ὑποστρέψω εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον·
11:24.targetText: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’

groups.note: The generic article is rendered an.
The generic article is rendered a.
English repeats the object rest as it after find.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB says the house I left and leaves μου ("my") and ὅθεν ("from where") implicit, as in Matthew 12:44.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.

11:25.sourceText: καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.
11:25.targetText: On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts the sentence with On its return and leaves καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the object; the Greek leaves it understood from 11:24.

11:26.sourceText: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτά, καὶ εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ, καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.
11:26.targetText: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle εἰσελθόντα, rendered they go in, to the main verb.

11:27.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας.
11:27.targetText: As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Blessed is the womb that bore You, and blessed are the breasts that nursed You!”

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive is a temporal "as".
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").
BSB repeats blessed in the second clause, where the Greek leaves it understood.
ἐθήλασας ("you sucked") is rendered nursed You.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula Ἐγένετο δέ ("and it came about") untranslated.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") implicit after said.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐπάρασα, rendered raised, to the main verb.
English supplies the copula in the first beatitude.
English supplies the copula in the second beatitude.

11:28.sourceText: αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.
11:28.targetText: But He replied, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”

groups.note: English repeats the object as it after obey.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in the beatitude.

11:29.sourceText: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν· σημεῖον ζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ.
11:29.targetText: As the crowds were increasing, Jesus said, “This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.

groups.note: ἤρξατο λέγειν ("began to say") is rendered said.
σημεῖον οὐ ("no sign") is rendered none.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated; As belongs to the genitive absolute.
BSB shortens "this generation is a wicked generation" to This is a wicked generation, so the subject's article and noun have no separate English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb.

11:30.sourceText: καθὼς γὰρ ἐγένετο Ἰωνᾶς τοῖς Νινευείταις σημεῖον, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ.
11:30.targetText: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
BSB repeats a sign in the second clause, where the Greek leaves it understood.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:31.sourceText: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτούς· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.
11:31.targetText: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has none.

11:32.sourceText: ἄνδρες Νινευεῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.
11:32.targetText: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.

groups.note: Νινευεῖται ("Ninevites"), in apposition to men, is rendered of Nineveh; BSB's Greek spells the name differently.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has none.

11:33.sourceText: Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ φέγγος βλέπωσιν.
11:33.targetText: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.

groups.note: BSB repeats the verb as he sets in the second clause, where the Greek leaves τίθησιν understood.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἅψας, rendered lights, to the main verb.
English supplies an object for puts.
English supplies an object for sets.

11:34.sourceText: ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου. ὅταν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ᾖ, καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινόν ἐστιν· ἐπὰν δὲ πονηρὸς ᾖ, καὶ τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινόν.
11:34.targetText: Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light. But when they are bad, your body is full of darkness.

groups.note: The article is rendered with the possessive your.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves this καί ("also") untranslated in the second clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has none in this clause.

11:35.sourceText: σκόπει οὖν μὴ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν.
11:35.targetText: Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness.

groups.note: μή ("lest") is rendered that … not.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

11:36.sourceText: εἰ οὖν τὸ σῶμά σου ὅλον φωτεινόν, μὴ ἔχον μέρος τι σκοτεινόν, ἔσται φωτεινὸν ὅλον ὡς ὅταν ὁ λύχνος τῇ ἀστραπῇ φωτίζῃ σε.

groups.note: μὴ … τι ("not … any") is rendered no.
The participle ἔχον ("having") is rendered with.
ἔσται ("it will be") is rendered you will be.
φωτεινὸν ὅλον ("wholly full of light") is rendered radiant.
ὡς ὅταν ("as when") is rendered as though.

φωτίζῃ … τῇ ἀστραπῇ ("lights … with its beam") is rendered were shining.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek has none.
English supplies "of it" to refer back to the body.

11:37.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρ’ αὐτῷ· εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν.
11:37.targetText: As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.

groups.note: ἐν τῷ with the infinitive is a temporal "as".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated; As renders ἐν τῷ.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the infinitive.
English joins the participle εἰσελθών, rendered went in, to the main verb.

11:38.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν ὅτι οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου.
11:38.targetText: But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.

groups.note: ἐβαπτίσθη ("he washed himself") is rendered wash.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name; the Greek has only the verb.

11:39.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.
